subject: art-design
title: Drawing & Composition: Foundations
welcome_lead: Pick up your pencil and uncover the building blocks of drawing — line, tone and how artists arrange a page.
meta_desc: Foundations of GCSE drawing and composition: line types, tone, perspective, rule of thirds and focal points.
final_note: You now have the core vocabulary to look at any drawing and describe how it works.

concepts.def: Continuous line drawn around the edge of a form, without lifting the pencil.
Parallel lines used to add tone and shading to a drawing.
Layered hatching at different angles to darken tones.
Building tone with closely placed dots; used in pen-and-ink illustration.
Spectrum from lightest to darkest tones; develops realism and depth.
Quick loose sketch capturing pose and movement; warm-up for life drawing.

walkthroughs.body_html: Lines do different jobs. Contour lines describe edges; cross-contour lines wrap around form to show 3D shape; hatching and cross-hatching build tone using parallel marks; gestural lines are fast and capture energy or movement.

A full tonal range runs from the brightest highlight through mid-tone to the darkest core shadow, with reflected light bouncing back into shadow. Practice a 5-step tonal strip to train your eye before shading any object.

Divide the page into a 3x3 grid. Placing important features on the lines or intersections creates a more dynamic composition than centring everything. The strongest contrast or sharpest detail usually marks the focal point.
